title: 1. Relational database model
description: Week 2: Data modelling, business rules, redundancy, relational databases, keys, NULL and relational set operators.

items.question: Before creating tables for a new database, why would the designer draw a data model?

options.text: To provide a blueprint for the database

items.explanation: The model communicates the design before implementation, like an architect’s blueprint.

references.label: Week 2: Data modelling, p. 5
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 2 - Data Model & Relational Database Model 7 Oct 2026 StuVer.pdf

items.question: Which option is an attribute of Library Book in the table?
items.explanation: A library book is an entity; its ISBN describes it, just as its author and category do.

references.label: Week 2: Entities and attributes, p. 7
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 2 - Data Model & Relational Database Model 7 Oct 2026 StuVer.pdf

context.title: Library Book — illustrative rows using the slide’s attributes

items.question: Using the business rules in the table, which option correctly classifies relationships 1, 2 and 3, in that order? Read each pair from the first entity to the second.
items.explanation: 1. School–Headteacher is one-to-one: each school has one headteacher, and each headteacher leads one school. 2. School–Teacher is one-to-many: a school can have several teachers, but each teacher works at one school in this example. 3. Pupil–Lesson is many-to-many: a pupil can attend several lessons, and a lesson can have several pupils. A junction table records one pupil–lesson pairing per row.

references.label: Week 2: Data Model Basic Building Blocks — Relationships, p. 8
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 2 - Data Model & Relational Database Model 7 Oct 2026 StuVer.pdf

context.title: Relationship examples from the Week 2 slide
rows: Each school has one headteacher, and each headteacher leads one school.
A school can have many teachers, and each teacher works at one school.
A pupil can attend many lessons, and a lesson can have many pupils.

items.question: A business is defining rules for its customer invoices. Which proposed rule protects data integrity rather than changing how invoices are displayed?

options.text: Show invoices in a larger font
Give each customer invoice a unique identifying number

items.explanation: The uniqueness constraint prevents two invoices from receiving the same identifying number.

references.label: Week 2: Constraints, p. 9
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 2 - Data Model & Relational Database Model 7 Oct 2026 StuVer.pdf

items.question: A customer has not made any bookings today. Using the rules above, which proposed booking can the travel agency accept?

options.text: One booking with one agent, one travel package and one payment transaction
One booking with two agents, one travel package and one payment transaction
One booking with one agent, two travel packages and one payment transaction
One booking with one agent, one travel package and two payment transactions

items.explanation: A satisfies all four rules shown. The customer has not booked today, so this would be their first booking of the day. The booking has only one agent, one package and one payment transaction. B breaks the agent rule, C breaks the package rule, and D breaks the payment rule. The daily limit applies to the number of bookings per customer, not to the number of packages or payments in a booking.

references.label: Week 2: Travel agency case scenario — Business rules, p. 11
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 2 - Data Model & Relational Database Model 7 Oct 2026 StuVer.pdf

context.title: Travel agency — rules for this question
rows: A customer can make at most one booking per day.
A booking can be handled by only one agent.
Each booking must have exactly one package.
Each booking must have exactly one associated payment transaction.

items.question: A designer wants to show the main entities and their broad relationships without deciding how the database will store them. Which model is appropriate?
items.explanation: A conceptual model shows the entities and broad relationships without the detailed database structure.

references.label: Week 2: Conceptual data model, p. 17
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 2 - Data Model & Relational Database Model 7 Oct 2026 StuVer.pdf

items.question: Which model identifies key and non-key attributes without specifying a particular DBMS implementation?
items.explanation: A logical model adds attribute and key detail but does not depend on how a particular DBMS implements it.

references.label: Week 2: Logical data model, p. 18
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 2 - Data Model & Relational Database Model 7 Oct 2026 StuVer.pdf

items.question: In a physical data model, how are entity attributes represented?
items.explanation: The slide maps entities to tables and their attributes to columns.

references.label: Week 2: Physical data model, p. 19
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 2 - Data Model & Relational Database Model 7 Oct 2026 StuVer.pdf

items.question: What is data redundancy in the lecture?

options.text: The same data appearing in multiple records or places
Data that has not yet been entered
A distinct identifier for each record

items.explanation: Repeated copies of the same fact are redundant. If one copy changes and another does not, the records can disagree.

references.label: Week 2: Data redundancy, p. 20
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 2 - Data Model & Relational Database Model 7 Oct 2026 StuVer.pdf

items.question: How does the lecture distinguish a relational database from a flat-file database?

options.text: It stores everything in one unlinked table.
It groups data into entities stored in multiple linked tables.

items.explanation: A relational database represents entities in separate tables and links those tables instead of keeping everything in one flat file.

references.label: Week 2: Relational databases, p. 22
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 2 - Data Model & Relational Database Model 7 Oct 2026 StuVer.pdf

items.question: What is the role of a primary key?

options.text: To repeat a value in every row

items.explanation: A primary key identifies one record. Two records cannot share the same primary-key value.

references.label: Week 2: Keys, p. 24
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 2 - Data Model & Relational Database Model 7 Oct 2026 StuVer.pdf

items.question: NULL values: What can you conclude from the NULL in John’s Phone No. column?

options.text: John has a phone number but chose not to share it.
John does not have a phone number.
No phone number is recorded for John, and the table does not tell us why.

items.explanation: NULL represents a missing value, not zero. John’s number could be unknown, deliberately withheld, or not applicable. For example, a number not yet entered and a number withheld for privacy can both appear as NULL.

references.label: Week 2: Importance of NULL Value, p. 27
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 2 - Data Model & Relational Database Model 7 Oct 2026 StuVer.pdf
